Preface / 前言

Programmer, coder, developer—there are any number of titles used to describe people who create software, but what does it mean to be a software engineer? Despite the way software is often taught, being a software engineer is about far more than simply producing syntactically correct programs.

程序员、编码员、开发者——用来描述软件创造者的头衔有很多，但成为一名“软件工程师”究竟意味着什么？尽管软件常常是被那样教授的，但成为一名软件工程师，远远不止是写出语法正确的程序那么简单。

Boot camps and universities typically focus on the mechanical aspects of writing code, creating people who are well-versed in programming. The body of knowledge required today to be a successful software engineer goes beyond learning a programming language; you must be well-versed in the full lifecycle of a software product. You must have a comprehensive understanding of more than just the syntax and grammar of a programming language; you must be well-versed in testing, architecture, modeling, and more. You must know how to work effectively with legacy code and how to reliably and repeatedly deploy code to production. To excel, be promoted, and to work on the most interesting projects, you must move beyond merely writing code; you must apply engineering principles across the entire development process. Even in the era of artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic coding tools, you must have a solid grasp of the fundamentals to wield AI tools properly.

训练营和大学通常只关注写代码的机械层面，培养出来的是精通编程的人。而在今天，要成为一名成功的软件工程师，所需的知识体系早已超出“学一门编程语言”的范畴：你必须通晓软件产品的完整生命周期。你对编程语言的语法和语义不能只停留在一知半解，还必须精通测试、架构、建模等方方面面。你必须懂得如何高效地与遗留代码打交道，以及如何可靠、可重复地把代码部署到生产环境。想要脱颖而出、获得晋升、参与最有意思的项目，你就必须超越“单纯写代码”；你必须在整个开发过程中贯彻工程原则。即便身处人工智能（AI）与智能体编程工具的时代，你也必须扎实掌握基础，才能正确地驾驭这些 AI 工具。

There are many paths to becoming a software engineer, from associate’s and undergraduate programs in computer science to intensive boot camps to teach yourself (Figure P-1). Early in your software engineering career, it can feel like you’ve just taken your first steps into a larger world. It can be overwhelming. We know, we’ve been there! Regardless of your background, if you’re a newly minted practitioner, you soon discover there is a vast array of critical topics you weren’t taught as part of a standard curriculum and skills you don’t have, which prevents you from advancing to more senior roles.

成为软件工程师的路径有很多：从计算机科学的副学士、本科项目，到高强度的训练营，再到完全自学（图 P-1）。在软件工程职业生涯的早期，你会感觉自己仿佛刚刚踏入一个更广阔的世界。那种手足无措的感觉是真实存在的。我们懂，因为我们都经历过！无论你的背景如何，如果你是一名刚入行的从业者，很快就会发现：有大量关键话题并没有出现在标准课程里，有大量技能你并不具备，而正是这些东西阻碍你晋升到更高级别的岗位。

原书第 17 页

There is a gap between what you learn in a boot camp or a computer science degree and what you need to know to become a successful software engineer.¹ (Technical companies like Thoughtworks have stringent hiring practices, yet they still send their new hires through a boot camp, and they aren’t alone.) This book attempts to bridge that gap by giving you the context and grounding you need to chart your career path and helping you identify opportunities for personal and professional growth. Think of it as an onboarding guide for the early talent software engineer.

在训练营或计算机科学学位里学到的东西，与成为一名成功软件工程师所需掌握的东西之间，存在一道鸿沟。¹（像 Thoughtworks 这样的技术公司招聘门槛极高，却仍然会把新员工送进训练营，而且这么做的不止它一家。）本书试图弥合这道鸿沟：为你提供规划职业路径所需的背景与根基，并帮助你识别个人成长与职业发展的机会。你可以把它看作一本写给初出茅庐软件工程师的“入职指南”。

This book aims to be your guide on that journey, to show you the things you may not know you don’t know.

本书的目标，就是成为你这段旅程中的向导，带你看见那些你甚至不知道自己“不知道”的东西。

Who This Book Is For / 本书适用人群

This book is specifically designed for new software engineers. Our goal is to show you the bigger picture of what it takes to become a true software engineer, beyond “just coding,” and what it takes to advance your career.

本书专门为新晋软件工程师而写。我们的目标，是向你展现一幅更大的图景：成为一名真正的软件工程师、并推动职业发展，所需要的远不止“写代码”。

1 A contributing factor to the prevalence of imposter syndrome (discussed in Chapter 14) in the software industry.
这也是软件行业冒名顶替综合征（第 14 章讨论）普遍存在的一个促成因素。
原书第 18 页

But the fundamentals that we’ll discuss in this book aren’t just for beginners. Experienced engineers can also benefit from mastering these essential skills, especially if they’re looking to move up and take on more senior roles. Building a strong skill set is what will unlock opportunities for more responsibilities and promotion.

不过，本书讨论的这些基础并非只面向初学者。经验丰富的工程师同样能从掌握这些核心技能中受益，尤其是当你希望晋升、承担更高级别职责的时候。扎实的技能体系，才是解锁更多责任与晋升机会的钥匙。

What You Will Learn / 你将学到什么

What are the skills you need to succeed and thrive? What separates the beginner from the experienced software engineer? From reading code, to writing code that’s readable, to testing, to work–life balance, to learning to learn—we will tell you everything you need to know (and even some things you didn’t know you needed to know). Most software engineers learn these things through trial and error, sometimes costing their projects dearly. But it doesn’t have to be that way! These skills are the fundamentals of software engineering that will set you up for a successful career and—unlike the flavor-of-the-day framework or the trendy language—these skills will last a lifetime.

想要成功、想要蓬勃发展，你需要哪些技能？是什么把初学者和资深软件工程师区分开来？从阅读代码，到写出可读的代码，再到测试、工作与生活的平衡、学会学习——我们会把你需要知道的一切都告诉你（甚至包括一些你不知道自己需要知道的东西）。大多数软件工程师是靠反复试错学会这些的，有时代价惨重。但事情本不必如此！这些技能是软件工程的根基，会为你铺就成功的职业生涯；而且——与那些“今日红极、明日过气”的框架或时髦语言不同——这些技能受用终生。

While this book isn’t meant to be an in-depth guide to any one topic, it will show you the universe of topics within software engineering, so you have enough information to understand the basic concepts.

本书并非任何单一主题的深度指南，但它会带你领略软件工程这片“宇宙”的全貌，让你拥有足以理解基本概念的信息。

Throughout the book, we will share stories and experiences from our careers, giving you an opportunity to learn from our mistakes. Each chapter concludes with relevant resources and practical exercises to help you practice what you’ve learned. If a particular chapter resonates with you, we encourage you to dive in and explore the topic!

在全书中，我们会分享职业生涯中的故事与经历，让你有机会从我们的错误中学习。每章末尾都会给出相关资源和实践练习，帮助你把所学落地。如果某一章让你特别有共鸣，我们鼓励你顺着它深入挖掘、继续探索！

Navigating This Book / 如何阅读本书

Just as there is no one path to becoming a software engineer, there are many ways to approach this material. While most readers will likely begin by reading this book cover to cover, you can also “choose your own adventure” by reading chapters based on whatever topic interests you at the moment. As you progress in your career, tackle new projects, and encounter newly relevant topics, you may want to return to certain chapters for guidance.

正如成为软件工程师没有唯一路径一样，阅读本书的方式也有很多种。大多数读者可能会从头到尾通读，但你也可以“自己选择冒险”：根据当下感兴趣的话题挑章节读。随着你职业发展、接手新项目、遇到新的相关话题，你可能会想回到某些章节寻找指引。

The book is broken into four sections. Part 1 begins with the core skills you need to be a successful software engineer. Part 2 explores the various technical practices you will encounter on projects, while Part 3 dives into the nuances of designing and building software. Part 4 focuses on your career growth and steps you can follow to take control of your journey.

本书分为四个部分。第 1 部分从“成为成功软件工程师所需的核心技能”讲起；第 2 部分探讨你在项目中会遇到的各种技术实践；第 3 部分深入设计与构建软件的细微之处；第 4 部分聚焦你的职业成长，以及你可以用来掌控自己职业旅程的具体步骤。

原书第 19 页

Here’s what you’ll find in this book:

以下是本书各部分内容概览：

Part 1: Core Skills / 第 1 部分：核心技能

  • Chapter 1, “Programmer to Engineer”, discusses the varied paths to becoming a software engineer and emphasizes the importance of foundational skills.第 1 章《从程序员到工程师》讨论成为软件工程师的多种路径，并强调基础技能的重要性。
  • Chapter 2, “Reading Code”, is about how software engineers spend more time reading code than writing it. It provides strategies for navigating unfamiliar code.第 2 章《阅读代码》讲述软件工程师花在读代码上的时间远多于写代码，并给出在陌生代码中穿行的策略。
  • Chapter 3, “Writing Code”, is all about the importance of writing code that is readable and maintainable. In essence, it illustrates why it’s more important to write for the developer than the computer.第 3 章《编写代码》通篇讲写出可读、可维护代码的重要性。本质上，它阐明了为什么“为开发者而写”比“为计算机而写”更重要。

Part 2: Technical Practices / 第 2 部分：技术实践

  • Chapter 4, “Modeling”, dives into the role of software modeling, aka the box-and-line diagrams you have encountered (or will encounter) on many projects, as a crucial aspect of communication among software engineers.第 4 章《建模》深入探讨软件建模的作用——也就是你在许多项目上已经（或即将）遇到的那些“方框加连线图”——它是软件工程师之间沟通的关键环节。
  • Chapter 5, “Automated Testing”, covers the benefits of automated testing for code quality and developer confidence.第 5 章《自动化测试》讲解自动化测试对代码质量和开发者信心的收益。
  • Chapter 6, “Exploring and Modifying Unfamiliar Systems”, highlights strategies for effectively working with existing codebases. Whether you’re joining a new team or maintaining a legacy system, these skills will help you confidently contribute to any codebase.第 6 章《探索与改造陌生系统》重点讲解高效使用既有代码库的策略。无论你是加入新团队还是维护遗留系统，这些技能都能帮你自信地为任何代码库做贡献。

Part 3: Application Development and Design / 第 3 部分：应用开发与设计

  • Chapter 7, “User Interface Design”, is an overview of user interface design. It explains why understanding the user and applying design principles will help ensure that your software meets your users’ needs.第 7 章《用户界面设计》是对用户界面设计的概述。它解释了为什么理解用户、运用设计原则，能帮助你的软件真正满足用户需求。
  • Chapter 8, “Working with Data”, is all about working with data, something nearly every software application does in some manner. It covers the essential skills you need to know to make informed decisions about data in your applications.第 8 章《处理数据》通篇讲数据处理——几乎每一个软件应用都在以某种方式和数据打交道。它覆盖了在应用中就数据做出明智决策所需的核心技能。
  • Chapter 9, “Software Architecture”, explores the complexities of software architecture, giving you some insights into the architectural trade-offs involved in every software project.第 9 章《软件架构》探讨软件架构的复杂性，让你对每个软件项目中都存在的架构权衡有所认识。
  • Chapter 10, “To Production”, talks about taking code to production. It discusses the unpredictability of real users and environments, and outlines strategies for building production-ready code.第 10 章《走向生产环境》讲把代码送上生产。它讨论真实用户与真实环境的不可预测性，并勾勒出构建“可投产代码”的策略。
原书第 20 页

Part 4: Professional Development and Growth / 第 4 部分：职业发展与成长

  • Chapter 11, “Powering Up Your Productivity”, returns to your day-to-day work and the importance of building your personal toolkit.第 11 章《提升你的生产力》回到你的日常工作，讲构建个人工具箱的重要性。
  • Chapter 12, “Learning to Learn”, covers the importance of continuous learning. The chapter offers strategies for keeping up with an ever-changing field.第 12 章《学会学习》讲持续学习的重要性，并给出在这个瞬息万变的领域里保持跟进的策略。
  • Chapter 13, “Mastering Soft Skills in the Tech World”, dives into the importance of soft skills to your career. It discusses collaborative communication, influence, and stakeholder management.第 13 章《在技术世界掌握软技能》深入探讨软技能对你职业生涯的重要性，涵盖协作式沟通、影响力与干系人管理。
  • Chapter 14, “Career Management”, focuses on planning and navigating your software engineering career. It discusses finding what you’re passionate about, exploring career paths, and being deliberate with skill acquisition. It also covers building a professional network, acing interviews, and creating a work–life balance.第 14 章《职业管理》聚焦于规划和驾驭你的软件工程职业生涯。它讨论找到你的热情所在、探索职业路径、有意识地习得技能，还涵盖建立专业人脉、拿下面试、创造工作与生活的平衡。
  • Chapter 15, “The AI-Powered Software Engineer”, touches on one of the most disruptive topics in the software space today: AI.第 15 章《AI 赋能的软件工程师》触及当今软件领域最具颠覆性的话题之一：AI。

Although a dedicated chapter explores AI, its widespread impact on the software development lifecycle means you’ll find discussions of AI throughout the book.

虽然本书用一整章来探讨 AI，但由于它对软件开发生命周期的广泛影响，你会在全书各处都看到关于 AI 的讨论。

Conventions Used in This Book / 本书使用的体例

The following typographical conventions are used in this book:

本书使用以下排版体例：

  • Italic indicates new terms, URLs, email addresses, filenames, and file extensions.斜体表示新术语、URL、电子邮箱地址、文件名和文件扩展名。
  • Constant width is used for program listings, as well as within paragraphs to refer to program elements such as variable or function names, databases, data types, environment variables, statements, and keywords.等宽字体用于程序清单，以及在段落中指代程序元素，如变量名、函数名、数据库、数据类型、环境变量、语句和关键字。
  • Constant width bold shows commands or other text that should be typed literally by the user.等宽粗体表示需要用户原样输入的命令或其他文本。
  • Constant width italic shows text that should be replaced with user-supplied values or by values determined by context.等宽斜体表示应由用户提供的值、或由上下文决定的值来替换的文本。
